# ALS SubZero: Complete Technical Reference

Designed and built by Samin Sami (ALS = "Al Sami", from Samin Yasar AL Sami).
Repository: https://github.com/Saminsami73/als-subzero
License: MIT

## 1. System Summary

ALS SubZero stores digital files in flight across computer networks instead of storing them on physical disks. The architecture revives the concept of acoustic mercury delay-line memory used in early computers such as the EDSAC (1949) and UNIVAC (1953), translating physical sound delay into IP packet propagation delay.

The total data capacity of any network link is governed by the Bandwidth-Delay Product (BDP):
Capacity (bits) = Usable Bandwidth (bps) * Round-Trip Time (seconds)

For example, a 1 Gbps link with a 40 ms round-trip latency holds 5.0 megabytes in flight.

## 2. ALS1 Binary Protocol Frame Specification

Every packet in flight carries a fixed 24-byte binary header packed in network byte order (Big Endian), followed by the payload:

| Offset | Type | Field Name | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0..3 | 4 bytes | Magic | ASCII "ALS1" (0x41 0x4C 0x53 0x31) |
| 4..5 | 2 bytes | Version | Major.minor (0x0100 for version 1.0) |
| 6..7 | 2 bytes | Flags | Bit 0: Parity chunk flag, Bits 1..15: Reserved |
| 8..11 | 4 bytes | Inode ID | Virtual filesystem inode index |
| 12..15 | 4 bytes | Chunk Index | Sequential block offset within file |
| 16..17 | 2 bytes | Payload Length | Byte count of payload (0..4096) |
| 18..19 | 2 bytes | Hop Count | Number of round-trip loops completed |
| 20..23 | 4 bytes | Checksum | Castagnoli CRC32C over header + payload |

## 3. Cauchy Reed-Solomon Erasure Coding

To survive network packet drops without disk storage, ALS SubZero uses Cauchy Reed-Solomon error correction over Galois Field GF(2^8):
- Irreducible polynomial: P(x) = x^8 + x^4 + x^3 + x^2 + 1 (0x11D / 285)
- Standard ratio: K=4 data chunks, M=2 parity chunks per stripe
- Generator matrix: A = [a_{i,j}] = 1 / (x_i XOR y_j) where x_i and y_j are distinct field elements
- Property: Any square submatrix of a Cauchy matrix is invertible over GF(2^8)
- Resilience: Any K surviving chunks out of K + M are sufficient to reconstruct all lost data chunks

## 4. Microsecond Departure Pacing

To prevent network socket overflow when round-trip times are low (e.g. sub-millisecond LAN paths), the engine includes a microsecond departure pacer:
- Priority queue ordered by scheduled release timestamp
- Equation: t_release = t_now + (T_target - (t_now - t_epoch))
- Enforces minimum spacing of 100 microseconds between consecutive packet departures
- Prevents burst drops and queue exhaustion

## 5. Verification Commands

1. Unit tests:
   `python tests/run_all.py` (20 tests verifying framing, CRC32C, Cauchy FEC, pacer, VFS)
2. Benchmark:
   `python scripts/run_benchmark.py` (tests 0%, 2%, 5%, and 10% packet drop rates with 100% data recovery)
3. Demo:
   `python scripts/run_demo.py` (runs a live 5-step demonstration with animated circulation metrics)
